action_items: OPTIONAL/MINOR: When anonymous visitor presses Esc in PresentationMode, the app navigates to '/' which is an authed surface and the route guard sends them to /auth/login. This is expected app-routing behavior (the F.2 fix is intact), but UX-wise a public visitor closing a share-link presentation lands on the login form. Consider routing Esc on public PublicPresentation to a 'thank you' / share landing page or simply window.close()/no-op for public surfaces. NOT a regression.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend fix at /app/backend/routers/moodboards_v1.py line 263-264: GET /_meta/presentation_transitions correctly drops Depends(require_permission(...)) and is now anonymous-accessible — verified curl HTTP 200, exactly 6 transitions returned. Sibling /_meta/page_presets and /_meta/page_skeletons still require auth (curl HTTP 401), so the change is correctly scoped.

Frontend fix at /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js lines 29-44: interceptor now checks window.location.pathname against a whitelist (/presentation/*, /moodboard/share/*, /f/*, /form/*, /auth/login) and skips both the localStorage wipe AND the hard redirect to /auth/login when on a public surface. Verified: protected paths (/dashboard) still redirect, public path (/presentation/{token}) does not. Clean, minimal, and prevents future public surfaces from being torn out.

Public PresentationMode UI mounts with no auth — CONCEPT chapter label, page counter 1/11, Chapters button + close button render. ArrowRight keeps overlay mounted (advance worked). Esc handler still navigates to '/' which then 401-bounces, but that is route-level behavior outside the scope of this fix.

rca of the issue: FIXED. Original RCA: PublicPresentation.jsx fetched /_meta/presentation_transitions which required auth → 401 → global axios interceptor force-redirected to /auth/login. Resolution applied by main agent: (a) removed Depends(require_permission) from the transitions endpoint (it returns a purely static registry, no tenant data, no PII), (b) hardened the axios response interceptor in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js to inspect window.location.pathname and skip the redirect/storage-wipe when the visitor is on a known public surface. Both layers of defense in place — even a future stray 401 from another auth-gated call on a public route will no longer punt the visitor out.
